title: Galivelop-workflow project config (.claude/gw.json)
description: Everything that varies between projects using Galivelop-workflow. Read only by scripts/config.py.

version.description: Workflow version the project was applied with.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the gw.json format; absent = 0 (written before 0.5). An older one is migrated in memory by config.py and written by /gw-update; a newer one than the workflow knows fails closed.

visibleLanguages.description: Languages every user-visible text must exist in (REVIEW.md).

log.description: Hand-off log path, relative to the repo root. Absent: docs/handoff.md, or the old docs/traspaso.md when only that exists (0.x; /gw-update moves it).

logSize.description: Cap on the size of the whole hand-off log, in characters (0 = no cap). handoff.py check warns above it and context_guard.py names the log as the culprit; handoff.py archive moves the Pending items of published versions out.

logArchive.description: Repo-relative path of the file handoff.py archive moves the Pending items of published versions to. It is not read at session start.

keepLegacyPaths.description: true: the project keeps its old Spanish paths (docs/traspaso.md, docs/registros/, docs/propuestas/), written explicitly in this file; apply.py then plans no move of them. `apply.py --keep-paths` sets it.

logRows.description: One row per branch with a size limit (handoff.py).

pushToProtected.description: How code reaches the protected branch. Both modes: pre-push requires the review mark on any direct push that brings code. pr: the PreToolUse hook also guards PR create/merge.

install.description: Commands that install dependencies (run in cloud sessions and CI).

ciInstall.description: Commands that install dependencies in CI only (the CI template runs them instead of `install`). Absent: CI runs `install`; [] : CI installs nothing.

setup.description: Commands run in cloud sessions after every `install` command, one after another (e.g. a build or a database seed); rerun only when `install` reruns.

check.description: Commands run in order on the commit being pushed; all must pass.

checkWrapper.description: Prefix put before every `check` and `relatedTests` command (e.g. tools/qa/host.sh); empty for none.

checkLockWait.description: Seconds scripts/check.sh waits for another check that holds the lock (<git common dir>/gw/check.lock) before exiting 3 and naming its pid and sha; 0 = do not wait.

checkReuseMark.description: The pre-push skips its check on a commit that only adds or edits the reviewMark file on top of a parent whose tree is recorded green (the commit scripts/reviewed.sh makes); false runs the check on it.

checkCacheInputs.description: Files (relative to the repo root, no '..') whose content is part of the check-cache key, for ignored files the check reads and the git tree does not see; a missing file counts as absent; [] = the key is the tree alone.

checkOutputGrace.description: Seconds scripts/check.sh waits, after a command ends, for the output it was copying to the log; a command that leaves a background process holding the output cannot hang the check longer than this.

worktreeLinks.description: Paths (relative to the repo root, no '..') the pre-push symlinks from the main checkout into the temporary worktree where it runs `check`; a missing source is skipped.

worktreeDir.description: Folder (absolute, or relative to the repo root) under which the pre-push creates its temporary worktrees, for a sandbox that cannot see $TMPDIR; empty for ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}.

reviewMark.description: Committed file holding the reviewed commit sha. Absent: docs/records/reviewed.txt, or the old docs/registros/revisado.txt when only that exists (0.x; /gw-update moves it).

recordsDir.description: Repo-relative folder where the workflow's skills write their reports (retro-*.md, opt-tokens and opt-ai reports, release texts). Absent: docs/records, or the old docs/registros when only that exists (0.x; /gw-update moves it).

proposalsDir.description: Repo-relative folder where gw-harvest writes its `# Harvest` files (and state.json), which `version.py --release` requires. Absent: docs/proposals, or the old docs/propuestas when only that exists (0.x; /gw-update moves it).

requireRetro.description: reviewed.sh requires a retro with a decided status on the branch.

agentSignatures.description: false: the commit-msg hook rejects agent signatures (a Co-Authored-By of a Claude model or with noreply@anthropic.com, Claude-Session, lines starting with "Generated with Claude Code" or a claude.ai/code/session link).

commitFormat.description: Format of the first line of a commit message: free (any) or conventional (`type(scope)!: text`, checked by the commit-msg hook; WIP: and the lines git writes itself pass).

commitRefs.description: true: the commit-msg hook requires a `Refs: <task id>` trailer (ids separated by commas) whose ids open an entry in refsSources; merges, reverts, cherry-picks and rebases are exempt.

commitNext.description: true: the commit-msg hook requires a non-empty next-step trailer in the last paragraph (`Siguiente:` with language es, `Next:` with en); GW_NO_NEXT=1 skips it for one commit; merges, reverts, cherry-picks, rebases and fixup!/squash!/amend!/Revert lines are exempt, and merge-branch.sh requires it in its message.

refsSources.description: Repo-relative files or folders (their tracked .md files) whose entries (table rows or list items) give the valid ids of `Refs:`, read from the index. Empty: `plan` plus `log`.

ciLocalLog.description: Repo-relative file where `ci-local.py --record` records each local run of the GitHub CI (a Markdown file; absent: docs/records/ci-local.md, or the old docs/registros/ci-local.md when only that exists). The PR hook takes a green line of it, whose commit has only content after it, as the CI that GitHub did not start (no Actions quota, no runners); it is never code for is-code.sh.

ciLocalWorkflows.description: Repo-relative workflow files that `ci-local.py` runs, whatever their triggers; empty: every .github/workflows/*.yml|yaml triggered by the event.

ciKeepSteps.description: true: apply.py never replaces .github/workflows/check.yml when it has lines of the project's own (steps, Node version, cache...) that neither the template nor an earlier one has, not even with --update; it writes check.yml.gw-new and says how to merge. false: the old behaviour (an older copy is replaced).

legacyNames.description: true: apply.py lists, as warnings with file:line, the uses of the pre-A8 Spanish names (scripts, skill folders, notes, comprobar.yml, docs/traspaso.md...) in the project's own text files. false: no listing.

legacyNamesSkip.description: Globs (fnmatch, on the repo-relative path) of files apply.py never lists old-name uses in, as history that is not renamed. The log, recordsDir and proposalsDir are always skipped.

legacyNamesMax.description: Most old-name uses apply.py lists per run (the rest is counted).

ciPython.description: Python versions the CI template runs as a matrix (non-empty strings without spaces, e.g. ["3.10", "3.13"]; quote them so 3.10 is not read as 3.1). Absent: one job with "3.x". Not [] (use no key).

ciIgnore.description: Names of foreign CI checks (a check-run name or a commit status context, e.g. a deploy) that do not block the merge nor count as the project's CI. An exact name, or a name with `*` for any text (`vercel*`); case matters; no regex. An ignored check never turns a red or pending check of the project into green, and a commit where only ignored checks reported counts as no CI.

releaseDocs.description: Repo-relative files that must name the version being released as a backticked token (`X.Y.Z`), read from HEAD: `version.py --release` fails when one is missing or still shows another version (a README status or what's-new section). [] checks nothing.

marketingSheets.description: One-page presentation sheets written in Markdown: mkt-sheet.py turns each source (repo-relative .md) into <outDir>/<parent folder>/<stem>.html and .pdf and checks they match the source. css: repo-relative stylesheet embedded instead of the built-in one (its relative url(...) are rewritten per HTML); timeout: seconds Chromium may take to print all sheets. A missing inner key takes its default. No sources: the feature is off.

nonTestExtensions.description: File extensions (lower case, no dot; the file's own extension is compared in lower case) of text and data files that red-without-fix.sh does not search for test code, so prose such as `improve it (URL)` is not mistaken for an `it(` test. A file with no extension is always searched. [] searches every file. Some stacks keep tests in .md/.txt (doctest) or .yml/.yaml (specs): remove those extensions from the list, otherwise an uncommitted test there is skipped and stashed with the fix.

content.description: Regexes (on repo-relative paths) of files that are content, not code: they need no code review.

logSections.description: Headings of the log sections recover.py --state shows after a compaction or /clear (without logRows). Empty: the first section and the one named Pendiente/Pending. After a compaction only the first section is shown.

protectedPaths.description: Path prefixes an agent (CLAUDECODE=1) may not commit; pre-commit refuses them.

staleRefs.description: Case-insensitive regexes that must not appear in docs (md-links.py): a list, or {"patterns": [...], "skip": [globs]} where skip lists repo-relative files or folders the check does not read (`*` stays inside a folder, `**` crosses; a trailing / means the whole folder).

linkRoots.description: Folders (relative to the repo root, no '..') whose Markdown files write relative links from the repo root instead of from their own folder (md-links.py).

scoutDir.description: Folder (relative to the repo root, no '..') where gw-scout-updates keeps its memory: architecture.md, proposals.md and the reports.

command.description: The command; {files} is replaced by the changed files that apply.

paths.description: Regex (Python syntax) searched in each changed repo-relative path; the command runs only if one matches, and {files} holds only those.

cwd.description: Folder of the repo the command runs in; {files} arrive relative to it (files outside it are left out). No leading / and no '..'.

command.description: The command; {files} is replaced by the changed files that apply.

paths.description: Regex (Python syntax) searched in each changed repo-relative path; the command runs only if one matches, and {files} holds only those.

cwd.description: Folder of the repo the command runs in; {files} arrive relative to it (files outside it are left out). No leading / and no '..'.

relatedTests.description: Commands for tests of what changed; {files} is replaced by the changed files. Each entry is a string or {command, paths?, cwd?}.

plan.description: Plan or roadmap files/folders where tasks are ticked or struck through (handoff.py).

taskId.description: Regex of the project's task ids (handoff.py); default [A-Z]{2,5}-\d+.

path.description: The agent map file (relative to the repo root, no '..'); agent-map.py checks the paths it cites. Absent: docs/agent-map.md, and a project without that file is not an error; a path set here that does not exist is.

prefixes.description: Short path prefixes the map uses, each mapped to its real folder (relative, no '..'): {"b/": "backend/src/"} reads `b/a.ts` as backend/src/a.ts.

roots.description: Top-level folders whose references the map check always looks up, even when the folder is gone. By default a backtick token counts as a path when its first folder exists, it ends with `/` or its last part has a file extension.

agentMap.description: The agent map (docs/agent-map.md): where each contract lives and what implements it. Read by agent-map.py.

subagentCap.description: Subagents (Agent/Task calls) one session may launch before subagent-cap.py asks the user to check they are not looping, and again every 10 after.

instructionLines.description: Line limits of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, which every session loads whole: doctor.py warns above warn and fails above fail (warn must not be above fail).

contextGuard.description: Startup-context guard (B21): recover.py --state compares the first turn after a /clear or a compaction with the compaction cutoff (cutoff tokens, or 0 = window x autocompactShare) and warns above warn percent and alarms above alarm percent; a second startup over alarm after a compaction is a loop.

default.source: Anthropic API list prices checked 2026-11-09 (claude-api skill, cached 2026-10-06); cacheWrite = 1.25 x input (5-minute cache); claude-haiku-5-5: prompts up to 100K tokens, cacheRead assumed 0.1 x input

metrics.description: Token ledger (B1/B2/B3/B4): the Stop hook metrics.py record appends, per session, agent, model and UTC date, the tokens the Claude Code transcripts show to the repo-relative ledger path (JSON lines, tokens only, never money); record false turns the recording off. reports: repo-relative folder where metrics.py report --write saves the period reports (daily/, weekly/, monthly/, quarterly/). prices: dated tables of USD per million tokens per model (input, cacheWrite, cacheRead, output); a ledger row takes the newest table whose since is on or before its date, and the model key equal to its model or, failing that, the longest key that its model starts with followed by '-' (date suffixes); no table or no key = no price. A given prices replaces the whole default list.

privateCheck.description: private-check.py (pre-push, on what each push adds): key formats, e-mail addresses (emails, default true) other than the built-in example/noreply ones and allowEmails (public; private ones go in the local .claude/gw.local.json), and the privateNames of .claude/gw.local.json. false turns it all off; true is the defaults.
